display.title: Episode 126: The Whispering Droplets (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: Counting the Omer teaches how precious time is; then the story of Akiva, who began learning Torah at forty after water droplets wore a hole in a rock.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi's Sefirah program. He explains that during Sefiras HaOmer we simply count days, because every day is precious and each one should be better than the one before. Time is a gift from Hashem that can never be bought back, as the funny story of Miriam and her lost dime shows: crying over what is gone only wastes what we have now. After a nine-year-old guest leads the Shema in Studio 604, story time tells 'Never Too Late'. Akiva, forty years old and unlearned, is begged by his devoted wife Rachel to learn Torah. Unsure, he sits by a river and notices that soft drops of water have bored a hole through a hard rock, and he realizes the words of Torah can do the same to his heart. He becomes the great Rabbi Akiva with thousands of students, and gives the credit to Rachel. The mailbox brings a poem about Moshiach and letters about when children say the Twelve Pesukim, followed by a tape offer, a birthday wish, and, before Shavuos, a reminder to grown-ups about Torah classes by telephone.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem, so use every day well; and it is never too late to begin learning Torah, which softens even a heart of stone.
